items.text: The league spokesperson announced that the home and away matches between Tractor and Persepolis this season will be held without spectators. Additionally, 90% of the spectator capacity for the Tehran derby will be allocated to Esteghlal fans. Ticket sales for the Tehran derby will be limited to 80% of the capacity of the Naghsh-e Jahan Stadium.

The US Treasury Secretary said Washington wants to impose the toughest sanctions in history against the Islamic Republic and intends to overthrow it with this plan. Meanwhile, the US President announced the start of the heaviest economic operation against the Islamic Republic.

Scott Bessent, the US Treasury Secretary, reposted Trump's Truth Social post about the start of an "economic operation" against the Islamic Republic, writing on X that any remaining connection with Tehran would quickly lead a country to economic destruction. He had previously stated that maximum economic pressure likely means military conflict will not resume. Bessent also mentioned that coordinated economic isolation would be imposed.

Alireza Beiranvand has been selected as one of the adult quotas for the national U23 team in the Nagoya Asian Games. The National Olympic Committee announced that Asian Games medalists are exempt from military service. Beiranvand's military status is still unclear, and the Tractor CEO said he is currently not subject to conscription.
About 60 migrants arrived by boat at a crowded beach near La Manga, Spain. Some migrants jumped into the water and swam to the shore. This surprised tourists, and some of them left the area.

A photo of Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf during his trip to Iraq with the phrase "Persian Gulf" in the background was published. This caused a reaction from the Iraqi parliament speaker, Hebat Allah Al-Halbousi. Halbousi also published a similar photo with a different phrase.

JD Vance, the US Vice President, announced the start of a new phase in the economic war against Iran, emphasizing economic pressure as the most effective tool against the Iranian government. He stated that Iran has endured more economic pressure than the US and that this trend will continue. Earlier, Scott Bassett announced that harsher sanctions against Iran are forthcoming, which will lead to the regime's collapse.

CENTCOM announced that the aircraft carrier USS George Washington has entered the Arabian Sea and will soon replace the USS Abraham Lincoln. Additionally, American forces have altered the routes of 67 commercial ships as part of the naval blockade of Iran. This report was published by Marzieh Hosseini from Iran International.

Jamshid Barzegar stated that repression and war should not discourage the people of Iran. He emphasized that those who order crimes must be prosecuted. These remarks were broadcast in a program on Iran International TV.

JD Vance, Trump's deputy, said their main focus is to prevent the Islamic Republic from acquiring nuclear weapons. He added that the Islamic Republic is under significant economic pressure and they are trying to ensure it does not rebuild its nuclear program. He also noted that oil and gasoline prices have decreased compared to a few months ago.

The expansion of threats from the Islamic Republic to Europe has become a key topic of discussion on the continent. NATO has emphasized its readiness to confront any threats. Some experts have warned about the defense limitations of certain European countries.

Donald Trump, President of the United States, criticized the JCPOA, saying that if he had not canceled the deal, Iran would have obtained nuclear weapons and used them against Israel and Middle Eastern countries. Referring to the Islamic Republic's attacks on Saudi Arabia, Qatar, the UAE, Kuwait, and Bahrain, he said that if they had nuclear weapons, they would have used them against everyone. Trump also stated that reaching an agreement with Iran is difficult and emphasized that Iran can never have nuclear weapons.

Miad Maleki, former head of the US Treasury's sanctions targeting office, warned about the impact of the UAE cutting trade with Iran and Iran's shift in access to foreign currency. He stated that the US Treasury has targeted the Turkey-related sector before this shift is fully implemented. Further actions focusing on Turkey are expected.

Mark Dubowitz warned that the Islamic Republic might create a military crisis before the Israeli and US elections. He mentioned the possibility of a direct attack or through proxy forces. This attack could lead to intensified conflict and political and economic consequences.

Donald Trump signed an executive order directing federal agencies to facilitate increased commercial space launches. The White House aims to create capacity for at least 1,000 launches and spacecraft returns to the atmosphere by 2030. Plans also include returning astronauts to the moon by 2028 and establishing a lunar base by 2030.

Dan Bacon, a Republican member of the US Congress, stated that the best end to the Iran war is for the people to reclaim their country. He said Donald Trump's goal is to prevent Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons and to keep the Strait of Hormuz open. Bacon also called for targeting the IRGC and destabilizing the Iranian government.

The US House Foreign Affairs Committee stated that Donald Trump has placed Iran's economy under severe pressure with the strongest economic measures ever taken. The committee added that this decisive economic pressure will drastically reduce the regime's funding for 'terrorist' activities and bring it to its knees. The committee urged Trump to continue maximum pressure.

Reuters reported that ship passage through the Strait of Hormuz decreased on Thursday compared to the previous day. The number of cargo ships was seven, half the number on Wednesday. There were no very large crude oil or liquefied natural gas tankers among these ships.

Shayan Samiei said that a combination of military pressure, naval blockade, and sanctions can change the calculations of the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that this change occurs when the Iranian government believes the pressures are not temporary. Also, the Islamic Republic will retreat when the cost of resistance exceeds the cost of agreement.

Shahram Khaledi stated that the Islamic Republic is losing its traditional influence in Lebanon. Economic pressure on Tehran and Hezbollah's financial network is increasing. There is a possibility of expelling Islamic Republic diplomats from Lebanon, which could escalate tensions.

Denmark has banned the entry of 17 foreign religious preachers, including an Iranian cleric. Danish authorities stated that the bans were applied due to public order considerations. This news was reported by Mehran Abbassian.

Mohammad Qaedi said that the deployment of air defense systems or fighter jets that restrict the freedom of Israel's air force in Syria is one of Israel's main red lines. The likelihood of a direct military confrontation between Turkey and Israel is very low. However, tensions between the two countries could turn into a shadow war in Syria.

The Afghanistan 2026 conference is being held at the University of Melbourne with the participation of academics and policymakers. The main topics include the situation of women and girls, regional security, and forced migration. The conference discusses Afghanistan's future and the international community's interaction with the Taliban.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated at a meeting of Iranian and Iraqi economic activists in Baghdad that military power alone is not sustainable without economic growth and national production. He emphasized that security and economy are two complementary pillars that must advance together. Ghalibaf added that without security, investment will not come, and without a sustainable economy, security cannot be maintained.
A citizen sent a video showing a long gasoline queue on August 21 in front of a fuel station entrance in Ghasemabad, Mashhad. The video was sent to Iran International.

Hossein Aghaei said if the US can block the routes for circumventing sanctions and the financial networks of the Islamic Republic, economic pressure could lead to the regime's economic collapse. He added that such a collapse could pave the way for expanded protests and the activation of society against the Islamic Republic.

Mohammad Hossein Mesbah stated that according to the government's plan, each Iranian will receive a monthly gasoline quota of 30 liters. Ahmad Alavi criticized the plan as economically inefficient and not increasing production. He said the policy aims to suppress consumption and control dissatisfaction amid current economic challenges.

A citizen reported that on the early morning of August 21 near Amir Kabir Dam on Chalus Road, Basij forces clashed with people after firing warning shots. They insulted and beat several individuals. This report was sent to Iran International.

Abbas Pazouki, the communications deputy of Mohammad Reza Aref's office, denied the published statements about setting the 87,000 toman gasoline price. He said Aref has not made any numerical statements regarding new gasoline rates. The fuel consumption management issue is still under expert review and no final decision has been made.

Masoumeh Sarbanzadeh, a political prisoner, is serving her five-year sentence in Dolatabad Prison in Isfahan. She was arrested in Tir 1404 (June-July 2025) by security forces in Najafabad. Her charges include forming a group aimed at disrupting security.

The news agency 2 December published a cartoon titled "Houthis: Iran's arm in Yemen." The cartoon depicts the relationship between the Islamic Republic and the Houthis and their role in the Bab al-Mandab Strait. In the image, a cleric with the symbol of the Islamic Republic holds the collar of an armed dog symbolizing the Houthis.

The Iranian women's national volleyball team started the 2026 Asian Championship with a 3-1 victory over Taiwan. For the first time in history, the team joined the group of teams with over 100 points in the world ranking and ranked 41st globally. Elaheh Poursaleh was the top scorer for Iran with 25 points.

A citizen sent a video showing an argument between a chador-wearing woman supporting the government and another woman over dress code. The chador-wearing woman said she takes photos of women without government-approved dress and sends them to government agencies. The video was sent to Iran International.

Hossein Ali Haji Deligani stated that the killing of some commanders and officials occurred through infiltration. He mentioned that many representatives have signed the plan to counter foreign infiltration. He also added that the judiciary lacks specific laws to deal with infiltration and that criminalization is necessary.

A citizen told Iran International that due to a power outage, he has to continue working in the workshop using his mobile phone flashlight. This issue was shown in a video he sent. The power outage has caused problems in the workshop.

Tottenham and Manchester City have agreed on the transfer of Savinho for 75 million pounds. After medical examinations, Savinho will sign a long-term contract with Tottenham. Tottenham is also negotiating to sign Omar Marmoush.

Heydar Nekousirat, a political prisoner in Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, suffers from diabetes, kidney failure, and vision problems. Despite repeated requests, he has been deprived of specialized medical care and transfer to an outside hospital. Prison authorities have not taken any action to provide him with treatment.

Mostafa Khoshcheshm, a media analyst, suggested using smart naval mines to block the Florida Gulf. These remarks sparked reactions. Mining international waterways can have serious human, security, and legal consequences.

Ronaldinho, the former Brazilian football star, joined Ravenna in Italy's Serie C and acquired part of the club's shares. He arrived in Italy on Thursday, August 20, and participated in the player introduction ceremony. Ronaldinho will not play in the first match of the season and did not give a definite answer about playing or scoring.

The US Treasury Department sanctioned Hezbollah Lebanon and 10 members of a money transfer network affiliated with the group and the Islamic Republic. This network moved hundreds of millions of dollars using commercial flights between Iran, Lebanon, Turkey, and the UAE. The report was provided by Ashkan Safaei from Iran International.

The International Federation of Journalists condemned the new Iranian parliamentary plan criminalizing contact with certain foreign media and warned about its consequences for freedom of expression. The plan was approved on August 16 by 183 representatives. According to it, interviews with media based in the US and Israel will be criminalized.

Relatives of Yasin Beiranvand held his birthday celebration on his grave on August 20. Yasin Beiranvand, a 20-year-old from Khorramabad, died on March 9, 2026, after 67 days of injury during the December protests. The news of his death was delayed due to widespread internet outages.

Hamidreza Hajibabaei stated that building alternative pipelines to the Strait of Hormuz benefits the US and harms the Islamic Republic. He emphasized that the Islamic Republic should prevent the creation of these pipelines and oil exports. He also said pressure should be increased on the Gulf countries to make them work towards ending the war and accepting Tehran's conditions from the US.

Ata Hosseinian, an economic journalist, mentioned the plan to allocate 30 liters of gasoline monthly to each Iranian as a "fair distribution" of fuel subsidy. He warned that implementing this plan would impose very high inflation on the country within six months. This statement was published by Iran International.

Reports from various cities in Iran indicate worsening fuel shortages and closure of some gas stations. Long queues for gasoline have formed. The government is considering price increases and changes to the rationing system, but officials deny imminent implementation of these plans.

Ebrahim Pirayesh, executive secretary of the Bandar Imam Workers' House, reported a failed suicide attempt by a dismissed worker from Mahshahr petrochemicals. The approximately 35-year-old worker attempted suicide during a workers' gathering after not receiving answers about his demands, but was stopped by other workers. Livelihood problems and job uncertainty were cited as causes of this situation.

Ali Shirazi said that Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf's main concern about the intensification of US economic pressures is the possibility of a 'hunger uprising' in Iran. He added that with the tightening of ways to bypass sanctions, the Islamic Republic faces the risk of famine. Even having money may not guarantee access to essential goods.

Mohammad Saeedi, the Friday prayer leader of Qom, spoke on August 21 about concerns regarding population decline and social issues. He emphasized the need for collective effort to address problems and activate local mosques with the participation of youth and families of martyrs. He also highlighted the social role of mosques in solving community problems.

Arif Mirmousavi's immortal was hospitalized with injuries caused by batons, knives, and live bullets from officers and died on January 14. A video shows his sister kissing his tombstone and lighting a candle at night.

Alireza Beiranvand is not in the initial 50-player list of Iran's U23 football team for the Nagoya Asian Games and cannot be added according to the rules. He is also nearing the end of his educational exemption and will be subject to military service from Mehr 1405. Therefore, being in the U23 team cannot delay his military service.

The documentary "Court of History" was broadcast on Iran International, sparking discussions about transitional justice and punishment of Islamic Republic officials. Some consider execution necessary, while others suggest alternative punishments for rebuilding Iran. Some warned that lack of appropriate punishment could lead to chaos.

A speaker at nightly government gatherings in Tajrish Square, Tehran, said that someone told him there is a smell of burnt meat near the Supreme Leader's residence. He went there himself and confirmed the smell. This claim was made during the gatherings.

The Supreme Court confirmed the death sentence of Arghavan Fallahi, a 24-year-old political prisoner. The sentence was issued by Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court. Fallahi was arrested on charges of rebellion and was pressured for forced confession.

Fatemeh Jami, an environmental activist, has been held in Gorgan prison for over 53 days without judicial resolution. Her case is under review at the General and Revolutionary Prosecutor's Office of Gorgan, but no hearing has been held yet. This has been confirmed by a source close to her family.

Ali Tajernia, chairman of Esteghlal club, stated that the club will pursue the championship trophy of the past season through FIFA and AFC legal channels and will not give up its rights. He emphasized that the follow-ups are done without political lobbying and that discrimination must end. Tajernia also called the proposal for a three- or five-team tournament a tasteless joke.

Reports indicate a new wave of disciplinary actions at Khajeh Nasir al-Din Tusi University in Tehran. At least 40 students have been summoned to the disciplinary committee. These actions are extensive and recent.

Donald Trump shared a post from American lawyer David Shon stating that Trump gave the Islamic Republic every possible opportunity to change its behavior. Shon wrote that Trump wanted the Islamic Republic to stop supporting global terrorism and join civilized countries. The consequences of continuing the current path were also made clear to the Islamic Republic.

A worker in Delijan was injured due to unsafe working conditions and lack of safety measures. The incident occurred while the worker was performing his duties. The report was published by Harana News Agency.

The Instagram page Ravaq Dar al-Zekr, which published content about the grave of Ali Khamenei and his family members, was blocked by Instagram. This page covered news and images of the burial site of Ali Khamenei and his family members.

The film 'Court of History' by Jamshid Barzegar depicts the history of repression in the Islamic Republic in a condensed case. The film raises questions about how trials should be conducted in Iran after the Islamic Republic. It covers executions, torture, and suppression of protests from the 1980s to the present.

Cristiano Ronaldo returned to the field after more than 240 minutes of absence and scored in the 83rd minute of the Al-Nassr vs Al-Riyadh match. This was his first goal of the season and the 977th goal of his professional career. Ronaldo was the top scorer for Al-Nassr in the last season and missed the first two matches of the new season due to a late arrival.

Donald Trump reshared a post by American lawyer David Shon accusing the leaders of the Islamic Republic of illegal and terrorist behavior. Shon wrote that Trump gave many opportunities to the Islamic Republic to change its behavior, but they did not accept. He also said Trump is now implementing the consequences of the Islamic Republic's continued illegal path.

Shahram Jamali, a resident of Mahmoudabad, was transferred to Amol prison to serve a sentence of seven months and sixteen days. This transfer took place on August 10, 2026. The news was reported by HRANA news agency.

Ahmad Vahidi, commander of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, stated that increasing the defensive and offensive capabilities of the Islamic Republic must continue rapidly. He described this strategy as the only way to counter current and future enemy actions. Additionally, the production of defense and military products should be accelerated.
